# You are ready to teach {#sec-summary .unnumbered}

If you have worked through this handbook, you now have everything you need to run **Git for Scientists**.

You understand why the workshop is shaped the way it is: taught on a need-to-know basis, in a room that is safe to fail in, with collaboration at the center (@sec-philosophy). You know the journey runs from pre-course work through four hours of hands-on practice to a forward-looking wrap-up, and that learners pick up R and RStudio fluency, a first taste of Quarto, and reversibility as a habit as side benefits along the way (@sec-course-shape).

You have the setup in place: the accounts and software every learner and the instructor needs (Part 2), the three GitHub organizations and their repositories (@sec-create-orgs), and a published cohort website (@sec-website). You know how to run the day, from pre-flight checks (@sec-before) to the timed run of show (@sec-run-of-show).

And you know how to keep it going: spinning up the next cohort from the templates (@sec-new-iteration), and keeping the material a genuine Open Educational Resource through its license and citation (@sec-citation-license).

## What is still to come

Two things in this handbook are deliberately open-ended, and they are yours to develop:

- **The record of each iteration.** The four concept drawings are developed and in use (@sec-live-drawings, @sec-appendix-drawings); what stays open-ended is each cohort's own record: the learner concept maps (photographed with consent, @sec-run-of-show), any drawings a cohort adds, and the parked-problem list. Capture them as photos and notes attached to issues in the iteration org (@sec-three-orgs), so each cohort's specifics and learnings live alongside that cohort's material rather than getting lost.

- **The second part** on task and project management (GitHub Projects, issues, and milestones) is planned as another four-hour workshop that builds directly on these foundations. It is not developed yet, and is expected to live under the same website repository template as this part. A further workshop on agentic coding for collaboration and scientific work sits on a longer horizon as a separate effort; this workshop is its prerequisite too.
